title: ANDS Studio — Guided submission journey
walkthrough:
You land on a hero screen headed "File your ANDS with Health Canada — guided end to end." A paragraph explains that an Abbreviated New Drug Submission is a complex filing and that this walks you through it step by step. The primary button reads "Start my submission →." Below it, two chips offer "Managing several products? Open the dossier catalog" and "Portfolio roll-up," each showing a count when there are dossiers in progress. A line notes bilingual Module 1 and the EN + FR Product Monograph live inside each dossier, and a footer says your progress is saved automatically.

On a first visit you may instead see a gate titled "Two things Health Canada must issue you," listing the 5-digit Company ID (lead time ~2 weeks) and the permanent Dossier ID (issued on request via REP), each with an explanation and a Health Canada guidance link. A button reads "I understand — begin the journey →"; it is remembered so you are not re-prompted.

After starting, the screen splits into three columns. On the left, "Your filing journey" is a numbered rail of steps. The current step says "You're here," completed steps show a check and "Done," and later steps show a lock icon with a plain-language reason for why they are not yet open. You can click any unlocked step to revisit it.

The centre column is the active step card. Each shows an eyebrow like "Step 1 of 10," the step title, a one-line purpose, and a short teaching paragraph where regulatory terms are dashed-underlined — hovering or focusing one reveals its plain-language meaning. The first step, orientation, includes a "Tell me about your drug" panel: fields for your drug, what you're filing (Generic of an approved brand (ANDS), NDS, SANDS, SNDS, or DIN application), a dosage form dropdown, and a checkbox for a new use. A "Check my pathway" button returns a routing verdict. Later steps collect a Company ID, a Dossier ID and product type, applicant and drug-product details, then document assembly, validation, fees, review, signing, transmission, and tracking. Most steps end with a primary button ("Continue →" or a step-specific label) and a "Next:" pointer to the following step.

The right column tracks readiness. A "Submission tower" shows your five eCTD modules stacking as they fill, with a toggle between a "3D view" and a printable "Checklist," and a caption like "Module 1–5 — 2/5 complete." Below it, a "Readiness" card shows a "● READY TO FILE" or "● BLOCKED" badge, a count of filing steps complete with a percentage, and a progress bar. An expander asks "How is [x]% measured?" and lists each tracked step. When something blocks you, a section headed "The single thing standing between you and ready" names the blocker and offers a button to jump straight to it. When everything passes, a note says your package is ready to transmit.

The top bar carries the subtitle "guided ANDS filing," a status chip reading "Ready to file" or "[x]% ready," and a "Start over" button that clears your saved session. In the document-assembly step, an extra panel points you to a dossier's Module 1 for the bilingual labelling and Product Monograph, which are tracked per dossier rather than in this session.
